lines.text: Every Windows user has stared into the Blue Screen of Death. The popular legend says Microsoft picked blue because psychologists found it calms panicked users.
That story is completely false. The color was decided in 1991 by one engineer, solving an annoying personal problem.
John Vert was writing the Windows NT crash handler. When the kernel panics, display drivers are dead, leaving only raw 16-color VGA text mode.
Vert's development machine was a MIPS RISC workstation. Its hardware firmware booted into bright white text on a deep blue screen.
His favorite text editor, SlickEdit, also defaulted to white on blue. Vert spent his entire workday staring at blue terminals.
So when Vert coded the crash screen, he picked the exact same blue. That way, he could boot, write code, and crash his machine without the monitor ever flashing.
Thirty years later, over a billion PCs crash in that exact shade — not for psychology, but because one developer hated screen flicker.
